doc: The short default policy a new customer system starts with: eight plain rules and the few numbers a buyer may want to change. It is a view over autonomy/policy.json, never a second source of authority: bootstrap/bootstrap.py (validate_default_pack) fails the boot if a rule here promises more than the policy allows. Written to org/policy-pack.json on every bootstrap and served to the owner's dashboard.
applies_to: a system built on Ultrastable, on first start; the owner changes it by editing this file or the copy in their own repository

rules.say: The system works on its own and does not ask you to approve ordinary work.
It starts careful and earns more freedom only through verified results, and loses it after a failure.
It never spends money, signs anything or sends a message as you without your yes. It prepares the step and waits only for that.
It never reads, prints or moves a password or key. Secrets stay in the platform's secret store.
Outreach to other people is drafted, never sent, until you have switched it on. Opt-outs always win.
Every change can be undone: it deploys with a rollback and never deletes data that has no backup.
It checks its own work with a test you can see, and keeps a change only if the number it aimed at moved.
Its own safety checks, refusals and your overrides always win, and it never works around a refusal.
